name: ANSI/IEEE main bonding jumper symbol
summary: US-practice bonding jumper between the grounded neutral and the equipment grounding system at the service.
description: In North American practice the main bonding jumper connects the grounded conductor, the neutral, to the equipment grounding conductor and enclosure at the service equipment. Its function corresponds to the neutral-to-earth link in TN-C-S systems. Single-line diagrams show it at the service disconnect, and separately derived systems have a corresponding system bonding jumper.

This illustration is an independent explanation and not an IEEE graphic. Only one bond should exist per service or separately derived system. Sizing rules come from the applicable electrical code, and the drawing should state the conductor or strap size.
readingNotes: Locate the bond at the service or derived system source only.
Check for unwanted downstream neutral to ground bonds.
drawingChecklist: Show the jumper at the service equipment.
Show system bonding jumpers on separately derived systems.
distinction: A main bonding jumper bonds neutral and ground at the service; an equipment bonding jumper bonds metal parts together.
